raw_affiliation_strings: Lecturer at the University of Haifa (his mailing address: 5 Chauncy St., Cambridge, Mass. 02138, U.S.A.). He was educated at Queens College (B.A., 1985) and at Harvard University (Ph.D., 1992) and has been a research fellow at the Harvard Business School (1992–93) and held visiting appointments at Northwestern University's Kellogg Graduate School of Business (1993–95) and Tel‐Aviv University (1995–96). His research interests include Japanese social organization and the interface between marketing and urban society in industrial East Asia. Among his publications are “Marriage with the Proper Stranger: Arranged Marriage in Metropolitan Japan” (Ethnology 34:37–51), “The Endurance of Neighborhood Associations in a Japanese Commuter City” (Urban Anthropology 25:1–37), and “Rationality, Morality, and Free Trade: U.S.-Japan Trade Relations in Anthropological Perspective” (Dialectical Anthropology 28, in press). The present paper was submitted II VIII 97 and accepted 26 viii 97; the final version reached the Editor's office 2 X 97
